title: The Making of the Veilguard
dek: Six candidates submit to Kumai’s judgment, disagree over impossible choices and fight one another before they have a settled company. The Veilguard takes shape through the work that follows.

facts.People: Lady Severina Blackveil; the forming Veilguard
facts.Opening test: 14, Month of Namo’o, Year 3 · Oiche Arena
facts.Organization reported: 20, Month of Physisia, Year 3 · Old Earth Hills
facts.Candidates: Severina · Pelegia / Pin · Thorn · Camilla · Kasiri · Modeli
facts.Arena outcome: Kasiri wins; Kumai still asks the six to choose a leader
facts.Later consequence: Thorn’s retrieval, resurrection attempt and witnessed living recovery

body:
The new Vanguard does not begin as an already united band. It begins with six people summoned to an arena, an old soldier who thinks they are unready and a war none of them can afford to ignore. Becoming the Veilguard takes longer than winning his exercise.

Six people who have already been losing

The candidates enter the Oiche Arena on 14, Month of Namo’o, Year 3 with lives and obligations already underway. Pelegia, often called Pin, lands among the others. Kasiri is delighted to meet a warforged. Modeli looks exhausted from watching over a body. Camilla and Thorn have other work they consider more urgent than an arena bout; Severina arrives confident in her skills.

Kumai-218 greets them with an accusation: have they neglected training from cowardice or apathy? The answers turn sharp. Camilla lists actual threats they have faced and asks why he never seems to leave his arena. Thorn says she has been keeping Ryvyt’s shop and returning to the woods. Modeli asks him to teach before there is another corpse to watch over.

The veteran says the earlier Vanguard is scattered and failing, and reports that Nuru has tasked him with starting again with these six. His report includes claims about absent predecessors; it is not a final verdict on every older adventurer’s fate. The task he puts before the candidates is immediate: become able to work together where reputation alone has not been enough.

Leadership before anyone draws a weapon

Kumai begins with definitions. What are leadership, honor and wisdom? Pelegia speaks of being worthy of followers and aligning them toward a shared goal. Modeli begins with listening, including knowing when the best decision is to ask someone else for help. Camilla describes responsibility, discipline and sacrifice.

Thorn answers from the work of keeping people fed, alive and pointed in the same direction. Honor means keeping an agreement and watching the back one promised to watch. Wisdom means recognizing the danger in a tempting shortcut before it becomes another cave-in.

Severina says a leader must create structure and answer for failure without shifting blame. She values consistency and restraint. Kasiri distinguishes knowledge from experience and insists that different communities understand honor differently. The answers give the candidates ways to recognize one another’s values. They have not yet shown how those values survive a crisis.

The choices they resist

The next test is hypothetical. Kumai places an imperiled battalion, a beloved companion and a powerful relic in conflict, then asks what the candidates would save. Severina and Camilla choose the force for which they would be responsible. Kasiri prioritizes the many over the one and warns against treating a relic as more important than people. Pelegia looks toward winning the battle and trying to bring the fallen friend back afterward.

Thorn tries to divide the work: a small rescue party, a line held by the others and a leader pursuing the relic. Modeli rejects the forced alternatives and the idea that the gods would reduce their chosen to numbers. His refusal does not solve an actual battle. It tells the people listening what he fears surrendering in order to become a commander.

In another imagined council, an innocent scout can be condemned to preserve an alliance. Most candidates choose truth over that alliance; Pelegia offers a darker route through an engineered accident. Their final dilemma sets a forbidden sacrifice against a Death Knight. Camilla and Thorn offer their own blood if it can work. Modeli refuses to kill a living soldier to preserve a fallen friend. Severina, Kasiri and Pelegia accept using the already fallen under the stated conditions, with different explanations of duty and loss.

These are answers to Kumai’s scenarios, not deeds the six have carried out. Several object to missing information and artificial limits. Kumai is listening for how they bear a decision, while they are also judging the person who has framed it.

The people willing to follow her

Kumai asks whom they would trust as captain. Thorn initially says words are not enough. He presses: whose heart would she follow before their competence has been tested?

Kasiri names Severina without reservation, then Modeli for his compassion and refusal to waste lives. Pelegia chooses Severina. Camilla does too, citing duty and judgment rather than their shared Order. Thorn eventually names Severina or Modeli from having fought beside them. Modeli’s first trust goes to Thorn; he admits he does not know Pin well enough and distrusts what he understands of Hellknight oaths.

Severina names Kasiri and tries to describe how the others’ different skills could serve a company. Kumai questions friendship as a criterion, but acknowledges where the support has gathered. He tells Severina that the others seem to want her to lead. She has been chosen provisionally by people who do not agree on everything, and whose reasons for following her differ.

A victory that does not settle command

Kumai returns armed and announces a free-for-all in which he will participate. Modeli attacks to discover how he fails under pressure. Kasiri moves into the fighting with her armored gauntlets, while Severina tries to make the others consider tactics even as she fights them.

Pelegia’s flight, sudden disappearances and illusory doubles make him difficult to catch. Camilla urges someone to focus on him. Severina asks why attacks have been directed elsewhere if everyone recognizes that problem. Their argument exposes the difference between naming a threat and coordinating against it.

Thorn becomes a polar bear. Kasiri exchanges blows with Modeli, whose determination keeps him standing after his face is badly injured. He finally falls. Kumai is pulled out and revived by his automatons, then watches from outside the fight. His participation has not made him its winner.

The final exchange leaves Kasiri facing Thorn after Severina has fallen. Kasiri spends nearly all the magic she has left, sends repeated missiles into the bear’s form and finally brings Thorn down. The narrator confirms her victory and that everyone has been revived. She returns to the floor exhausted. Winning the exercise has shown her endurance and skill; it has not automatically made her the captain.

The test leaves them an argument

Kumai praises Kasiri, then tells them to discuss among themselves and find him a leader. The result is frustration. Camilla leaves saying there are real threats to address. Thorn is annoyed. Modeli can barely hear through his injuries and wants to return to the body he has been watching.

Severina asks them to calm down and consider what they have learned about one another’s strengths. Kasiri questions the point of a test whose examiner joined the fight and changed it. Severina takes her hand and suggests rest before another decision. The company is not founded by a seamless vote followed by universal contentment. It has to continue after a day that left its candidates bruised and disagreeing.

A name and the means to leave Prima

By 20, Month of Physisia, Kumai has summoned another company to the Old Earth Hills. The snow falls around people who have kept working since the arena. Moira and Karnak are present alongside earlier candidates and other companions; being at this test does not by itself establish a permanent faction roster.

Kumai wants results rather than praise or a medallion. Severina reports that she has gathered people, picked a name and started seeking equipment to reach other islands quickly. He dismisses the answer. She accepts that results matter and turns toward the work in front of them.

Before the coming fight she places Karnak, Kasiri, herself and Øblivion forward, with Camilla, Moira and Modeli behind and ready to adapt. Modeli considers the arrangement sensible for his abilities. Organization has begun to take a practical form: where people stand, who can support them and how they will answer danger beyond one settlement. The exact naming day remains unrecovered.

The name enters a wider conversation

On 25, Month of Physisia, Severina, Camilla and companions find Melian at the town hall, occupied with accounts and the consequences of trade. They want knowledge about the ruins they have explored and help approaching the Ahau. Melian does not know every ruin on the island and distinguishes what she knows from what the adventurers suppose.

Severina now speaks publicly of the Veilguard. It and the newer adventurers need help preparing for the Great War, she says. She wants to learn whether closer cooperation with a neighboring power is possible. Melian warns that the Ahau and Rahu are sheltered from that war and may dismiss it as distant tales.

The meeting leaves work rather than a completed defensive alliance. The adventurers agree to seek an ambassador; Melian sends a courier. Other questions concern evidence from the quarry and practical support for Pristinia’s building. When Severina offers the Veilguard’s help, Melian asks for materials. A company that means to fight across regions still has obligations among the people whose town supplies its foothold.

When bringing someone home becomes the work

Thorn’s later loss makes the company’s promises concrete. Severina and Pelegia’s established recovery discussions concern shared resources and bringing her home. In the recovered return, Severina carries Thorn’s body toward the Tower. Ryvyt works over it with alchemical preparations, and the narrator describes the party reaching safety.

Severina asks Alyhotep whether he can bring her back. He says he can use an arcane Wish to perform a resurrection and begins the attempt. By 8, Month of Nuru, Thorn is alive in the Tower, asking for warm tea in a scratchy voice. That living appearance establishes recovery, while the exact narrated instant of the spell’s completion remains absent.

She still feels dreadful and later says she died. Farkur offers rest without shame. Keeping a member means accepting the need for recovery as well as retrieving a body. The founding’s questions about lives, usefulness and responsibility now belong to people the company actually knows.

Work inherited, not completed

The founding has become more than a leadership exercise, but it has not ended danger or supplied every answer about Gael’s future. Fenwick’s later welcome, with his Knights affiliation explicitly retained, gives a witnessed example of the company growing without absorbing every other organization.

The Veilguard’s story continues through the people it must protect and the promises it must keep after failure. The founding record establishes chosen leadership, organization and a name; its later service shows what those choices begin to require.

People and places in this history The Veilguard · Lady Severina Blackveil · Thorn · Gael · Fenwick d'Jorasco
